segments.heading: Section 4.6: three visits in the 7200 MT/s boot
segments.text:
Continues the function `section4` that starts at line 24. These lines write the heading of section 4.6.
- Lines 1042 to 1615 read no csv row and no csv column. They work on the interval records, and on the comparisons and record lists that lines 31 to 33 took from `c`.
- These lines call neither `cmps` nor `q2row`. So they add no range test to `V['q2_rows']`. The verdict texts of section 4.9 use the comparisons that were made before.
- A total rate is the field `GBps` of a record, in GB/s. Part A record: the csv column `aggregate_GBps`. bwx record: the sum over the threads of bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9 [Ref2].
- Section 4.7 uses two other fields of a bwx record: `mesh0_GBps` and `mesh1_GBps`, the sums per mesh (line 1221).

- `allv`: the asmread records of row F72d12, of part L and of control I, joined to one list. `facts_text.py` selected each list by `dataset` and `kernel`, with no position condition [Ref1]. In facts.json all of these records are at position 1. They are 2, 6 and 4 intervals.
- `av`: the lowest, the highest and the median rate of this list. Before this line `av` was a helper (line 825). From here it is a range.
- `kLI` compares part L with control I. `kIF` compares control I with F72d12. Here `compare` works on two lists of the same 7200 MT/s boot.
- The build stops unless part L lies above control I and control I lies above F72d12, both without overlap.
`tI` and `tL` hold the launch times of the two control I processes and of the three part L processes, from `evd`. The sentence that opens the section prints the first 8 characters of the boot id.

Writes the table of the three visits, one row per visit. `f72la` is the launch line of the F72d12 process. `fenv` is the parsed env.txt of its folder (lines 38 and 39).
- Launch times and start state: from `f72la` and `fenv` for F72d12, from `evd` for part L and control I. The control I row also prints the highest %CPU value of its two process lists, from the env.txt entries of `D['X']`.
- The part L row prints the lowest and the highest load at launch of its three processes. Its gap after part A is the gap of T72L1 alone, here and in lines 1168, 1338 and 1581. None of these lines reads the gaps of T72L2 and T72L3. In facts.json the three gaps are equal (5 s).
- The F72d12 row prints the first entry of the process list in env.txt. `facts_data.py` describes this list as sorted by %CPU, highest first [Ref2].
- Time since the first Linux kernel log line of the boot: launch time minus `try6['first_log_utc']`, printed by `dur`.
- `asmread, GB/s` and `oldread, GB/s`: the lowest to the highest `GBps` of the list, with 2 decimal places. No mean is taken.
- `n per kernel`: intervals / processes. The code counts the asmread list only.

- `spread`: the highest minus the lowest asmread rate of the three visits, in GB/s. In the present sheet the two rates are 327.93 and 301.90 GB/s, and `spread` prints as 26.03 GB/s [Ref4].
- `ov`: the range of the oldread intervals of the three visits.
- Line 1072 writes fixed words: the three asmread ranges do not overlap each other. The check in line 1048 tests them.
- Line 1073: the build stops unless the lowest asmread rate belongs to F72d12 and the highest to part L. Line 1074: the same check for oldread, with the lowest rate in part L and the highest in control I.
- The percent value of the bullet is `spread / av['lo'] * 100`. That is the spread as a percent of the lowest rate (8.6 % in the present sheet).
- `kIF['dist']`: the lowest control I rate minus the highest F72d12 rate (11.00 GB/s in the present sheet). The words "launched at a load below 1.0" of line 1078 are typed in the template. The check in line 898 tests them for control I. No check tests them for F72d12. In facts.json its load at launch is 0.34.

No rate is used in these lines. They compare the process lists of F72d12 and of control I.
- `envI`: tag, highest %CPU and path of env.txt for each control I process.
- `t_env`: the seconds from the first Linux kernel log line of the boot to the date line of env.txt of F72d12.
- The build stops unless `t_env` is positive, the first entry of the F72d12 list has more than 10 %CPU, and every control I list stays below 1 %CPU.
- The bullet prints the first two entries of the F72d12 list with their line numbers in env.txt, and the highest %CPU value of the control I lists.

A hypothesis on the first entry of the F72d12 process list, a thread with a high %CPU value. No rate is used.
- `gt`: the process-list lines of gaps.txt that hold the command name of that first entry. The build stops unless exactly one exists and gaps.txt holds an `uptime` line. That line gives the time of day at which gaps.txt was written [Ref2].
- `t_gap`: the seconds from the first Linux kernel log line to that time.
- `cpu1`, `cpu2`: %CPU / 100 x seconds since the first Linux kernel log line. Each is an estimate (est.) of the CPU time of the thread in seconds, at one of the two readings. It assumes that the thread started at that log line.
- `f72end`: the time of the rc line of the F72d12 process.
- The build stops unless the F72d12 process ran between the two readings and `cpu2` is above `cpu1`.

- The oldread bullet prints `ov['hi'] - ov['lo']` in GB/s, and the same value as a percent of the lowest oldread rate. Present values: 7.59 GB/s and 1.6 % [Ref4].
- `b12`: the range of `P12a`, asmread at position 1 of the 8000 MT/s rows L-1 to L-4. The bullet prints the range, its width `hi - lo` in GB/s, and n.

- `lo_all`: every record of the runner bwx rows B7a, B7b, C3a and C3b whose kernel is read or asmread. The selection has no position condition. `bxa` is the range of this list (192 intervals of 24 processes in the present sheet [Ref4]).
- The bullet for rule V1 point 5 prints four highest rates at 8000 MT/s. Two are bw_new read and bw_new asmread over rows A-1 and A-2 together. Two are read and asmread over the four runner bwx rows.
- Each of the four is `rng(...)['hi']`, the largest `GBps` of the selected records.
- Rule V1 point 5 forbids the use of 280 to 310 GB/s as the 8000 MT/s range of the new kernel [Ref5].

- `b5rev`: every record of rows B5a-rev and B5b-rev. `top_r` and `top_a` are the single records with the highest rate of kernel read and of kernel asmread among them.
- `b5read`: the range of kernel read over the four B5 rows, forward and reverse.
- `gro`, `gra`: the 7200 MT/s ranges of the part C groups read after oldread and read after asmread.
- `in_(v, a)`: true when the value `v` lies inside the range `a`, ends included.
- First check: `top_r` and `top_a` are above the highest read rate and the highest asmread rate of rows B7a to C3b.
- Second check: `top_r` lies inside both part C ranges, and `top_a` lies inside the asmread range of part L. The build stops when a check fails.

- `where` describes one record as text: process tag, folder, position, kernel before, and the line of its I row in the csv file.
- The first bullet prints `top_r` and `top_a` with their source. It also prints the number of reverse-order processes (`rng(b5rev)['procs']`) and their interval length (`secs`).
- The same bullet prints the range `b5read` and its number of processes. Rule F2 point 4 quotes this range.
- The second bullet prints the part C ranges and the part L range that hold the two values. It states that these values are not a like-for-like baseline.
- No new rate is computed.
- Two parts of the first bullet are typed in the template: the words "one interval per kernel, common stop" and the sentence on read_sparse and asmread2. No check tests them. In facts.json each of the 4 processes has one record for each of the kernels oldread, read and asmread. The field `stop` of every such record is `common`. The fields `kernel_before` of `top_r` and `top_a` are read_sparse and asmread2.

Six distances of asmread in GB/s. `aL`, `aF` and `aP` are the ranges of part L, of F72d12 and of the 8000 MT/s pool L-1 to L-4.
- `near_boot`: the lowest rate of part L minus the highest rate of F72d12. `near_pool`: `cLa['dist']`, the lowest rate of part L minus the highest rate of the pool.
- `med_boot`, `med_pool`: the median of part L minus the median of F72d12, and minus the median of the pool.
- `far_boot`, `far_pool`: the highest rate of part L minus the lowest rate of F72d12, and minus the lowest rate of the pool.
- Present values, pool first and boot second: 12.48 and 18.87 GB/s (nearest ends), 17.61 and 20.54 GB/s (medians), 39.38 and 26.03 GB/s (farthest ends) [Ref4].
- The build stops unless `far_boot` equals `spread`. It also stops unless the boot distance is the larger one for the nearest ends and for the medians, and the smaller one for the farthest ends.
- `c['dist']` keeps the six values for section 4.9 (line 1303).

The build stops unless both ends of the F72d12 asmread range lie inside the range of the pool L-1 to L-4 (`cFa`). The bullet prints three nearest-end distances in GB/s: F72d12 above L-1 alone (`kF1`, set in line 890), and part L and control I above the pool (`cLa`, `cIa`). Earlier checks test that each of the three distances is above 0 without overlap: line 891 (`kF1`), one check in `facts_text.py` (`cLa`) [Ref1] and line 889 (`cIa`).

- `hp_`, `ep_`: the process and the first hardware error record of the kind `possible` from section 4.1 (lines 295 and 304).
- `offset_s`: the journal time of the record minus the time of the launch line, in seconds. Both times are whole seconds. So the record lies at most `offset_s + 1` seconds after the process start [Ref3].
- The build stops unless the process belongs to row L-1 and `offset_s + 1` is at most 2 s.
- The bullet lists what differs between part L and row L-1. It uses no rate. Its count "2 corrected records" is typed in the template. Lines 245 and 293 test it.

Two bullets on the start state. No rate is computed.
- Control I against L-1: the load averages of the launch lines (`Ila` for control I, `l1la` for L-1), and the seconds since the last 120-thread process (`Igap`). The three names were set in lines 894 to 896. The check in line 898 tests the words "all below 1.0".
- The pool L-1 to L-4: `c['byst']['Ba']['procs']` is the number of pool processes that started after 120-thread work. `c['byst']['asm_near']` is the distance in GB/s by which part L lies above their asmread range. Both come from the view by start state (line 563). The check in line 560 tests that part L lies above this range without overlap.

- Lines 1179 to 1182: a summary bullet. Its words are fixed: the code inserts no measured value. Checks test its statements: line 748 (part A), one check in `facts_text.py` (part L) [Ref1], line 889 (control I) and line 1351 (part C).
- `xa1`: the cell of `pa3` for bw_new asmread, round 1. `xa1['s1']` holds its 3 intervals of session 1.
- `top2`: the interval with the highest rate of bw_new asmread in row A-2. Both rounds are searched.
- `low1`: the intervals of `xa1['s1']` whose rate is below the rate of `top2`.
- The build stops unless `top2` is a round-2 interval and `low1` is not empty.
- The bullet prints the count, the rates and the csv line numbers. In the present sheet 2 intervals (321.15 and 321.79 GB/s) lie below 321.87 GB/s [Ref4].

The text that rule V1 point 3 requires, from the 10-module rows.
- `x1`, `x1b`: the asmread records of rows X1d10 and X1d10b. In facts.json each row is one process with 2 asmread intervals.
- `apart`: (median of `x1b` / median of `x1` - 1) x 100, in percent. The median of 2 values is their mean. Present value: 9.4 % [Ref4].
- `o10`: the range of oldread over the three 10-module rows X1d10, X1d10b and BASEd10.
- `ins`: the text of the rule with the 4 asmread rates and `apart`. In line 288 the name `ins` was a list. From here it is this text.
- The text is appended to `V['insufficient_data']` and written as a bullet. Line 1554 later replaces that list.

- The bullet for rule V1 point 4 prints the oldread range `o10`, its width and n. The width is `width_pct(o10)` = (highest - lowest) / lowest x 100. Present values: 359.56 to 362.15 GB/s, 0.7 % wide, 6 intervals of 3 processes in 3 boots [Ref4].
- The build stops unless this width is below 1 %.
- `o10x`: the oldread range of each 10-module row alone. `o10p`: the range of X1d10 and X1d10b together.
- The last bullet states a limit: only X1d10 and X1d10b ran with the same firmware settings. It prints the width of `o10p` (0.5 % in the present sheet). The settings of each row are typed in the template. The check in line 198 tests only that the DIMM report holds the oldread rates of the three rows and two phrases on changed TXREQ settings.

segments.heading: Section 4.7: sums per mesh
segments.text:
Writes the heading and the first lines of section 4.7. The heading says that this view was looked at after the numbers were seen. It is not part of the rules that were fixed before the run.
- The thread counts of the text (64 on mesh 0, 56 on mesh 1) are typed in the template.
- Two integrity checks of `build_facts.py` test that every bwx record is an interval with 64 threads on CPUs 0-63 and 56 threads on CPUs 64-119 [Ref3]. Line 1461 stops the build when a check fails.

segments.heading: Helper `mrow`: one table row of mesh sums
segments.text:
Returns one table row for a list of bwx records `rs`.
- `mesh0_GBps` of a record: the sum of bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9 over the threads on CPUs 0-63 of one interval, in GB/s. `mesh1_GBps`: the same sum over the threads on CPUs 64 and higher [Ref2].
- `m0`, `m1`: the lowest and the highest value of each field over the list. No mean is taken.
- The row holds the label, the memory speed of the first record, the number of intervals, both ranges and the source files.

The lists that the two tables show, each as a pair of label and records.
- `sets_o` holds 7 oldread lists: part L, part C, control I, F72d12, `P12o` (pool L-1 to L-4, position 0), rows R0 and R0b at position 0, and every oldread record of the runner bwx rows.
- `sets_a` holds 11 lists of load-only kernels. Eight are at 7200 MT/s: asmread of part L, the five part C groups of `CG`, and asmread of control I and of F72d12.
- Three lists of `sets_a` are at 8000 MT/s: `P12a` (pool L-1 to L-4, position 1), rows R0 and R0b at position 1, and `lo_all` (line 1110).
- The two runner bwx selections have no position condition. Their labels name the positions. For `lo_all` the build stops unless its records are exactly read at positions 1 and 6 and asmread at positions 2 and 5.
- For oldread these lines do not check the label "positions 0 and 7". In facts.json the oldread records of these rows are at positions 0 and 7 only.

Writes two notes and the two tables.
- Each table row comes from `mrow`: the lowest to the highest mesh 0 sum and mesh 1 sum over the intervals of one list.
- The first table holds the 7 oldread lists of `sets_o`. The second table holds the 11 load-only lists of `sets_a`.
- Line 1244 says in fixed words that no bwx12 row at 8000 MT/s holds the kernel read. No check tests these words. In facts.json no bwx12 record at 8000 MT/s has the kernel `read`. The kernel sequences (`seq=`) in the header lines of the csv files that `build_facts.py` reads for these rows name no kernel `read` either.

The checks for the oldread statement of this section.
- `o72`: every oldread interval at 7200 MT/s, from part L, part C, control I and F72d12 (20 intervals in the present sheet).
- `o80`: oldread at position 0 of the bwx12 rows L-1 to L-4 and of the bwx11 rows R0 and R0b (18 intervals). `oxx`: oldread of the runner bwx rows (96 intervals) [Ref4].
- For each list `rng` gives the lowest and the highest `mesh0_GBps` and `mesh1_GBps`.
- The build stops unless two conditions hold. The lowest mesh 1 sum of `o72` is above the highest mesh 1 sum of `o80`. The highest mesh 0 sum of `o72` is below the lowest mesh 0 sum of `o80`.
- The same check runs for `o72n` (without part C) and for `o72p` (without part C and without control I).
- `c['mesh']` keeps the three interval counts for section 6 (line 1503).
Writes four bullets with the mesh 1 range and the mesh 0 range of `o72`, `o80`, `o72n` and `o72p`, each with its interval count. `F72_WHAT` is a fixed label for F72d12. No new value is computed.

- The check against the runner bwx rows (`m0_x`, `m1_x`). The build stops unless four conditions hold.
- With part C: the mesh 1 range and the mesh 0 range at 7200 MT/s both overlap the ranges of runner bwx.
- Without part C: the mesh 1 ranges overlap, and the highest mesh 0 sum at 7200 MT/s lies below the lowest mesh 0 sum of runner bwx.
- The bullet prints that last distance, `m0_x['lo'] - m0_n['hi']` (0.26 GB/s in the present sheet [Ref4]).
- The last bullet has fixed words. It says that the data do not show whether the memory speed changes the split.

segments.heading: Section 4.8: record-only table of the test loops
segments.text:
One table row per test loop (read_nop96, read_nop256, read_1pl). Four data columns, one per value of `dataset`: part L (`rerun-L`), control I, F72d12 and L-1.
- `sel` takes every record with that kernel and that `dataset`.
- A cell prints the lowest to the highest `GBps` and the number of intervals.
- The sheet makes no statement from this table.

segments.heading: Section 4.9: verdict for Q2
segments.text:
- Reads results of earlier sections from `c`. `by`: the start-state groups of the pool L-1 to L-4. `dist`: the six distances of line 1147. `oth`: the other-binary processes that started after 120-thread work. `pcv`: part C in the view by start state.
- `kF1`, `kI1`: asmread of F72d12 and of control I against L-1 alone.
- The build stops unless the first entry of the F72d12 process list has more than 10 %CPU.
- `c['f72_limit']`: one sentence on the limit of F72d12 as an idle start. The verdict for the new read kernel (line 1376) and section 0 quote it [Ref1].
- `side(k, n72)`: prints both sides of a comparison `k`. These are the 7200 MT/s range with `n72` (its n as text), and the 8000 MT/s range with its n.

segments.heading: Verdict text for the old read kernel
segments.text:
The template of `V['q2_old_read']`, the Q2 verdict for the old read kernel. Its statements, in order:
- Part A (bw_old read) and part C (oldread): the wording of the range test, both ranges, and the width of the 8000 MT/s range in percent.
- Part L (oldread): the wording, both ranges, and the distance of part L below the pool, at the nearest ends and between the medians.
- F72d12 and control I: their oldread ranges. The text says that they overlap the 8000 MT/s range.
- The view by start state: the pool processes that started after 120-thread work, and the distances of part L and of part C below them.
- The other-binary processes, the lowest oldread interval at 8000 MT/s, and the measurement that would resolve the open question (`H1_MEAS`).
- Earlier checks test fixed words of this text. `facts_text.py` stops the build before it calls `section4` unless parts A and C, control I and F72d12 overlap their 8000 MT/s range, and part L lies below the pool without overlap [Ref1]. The checks in lines 557 to 608 test the words on the view by start state, on the other-binary processes and on the lowest oldread interval at 8000 MT/s.

The values for the template, in the order of the text. This statement computes no new rate and no new distance. `nns` and `nn` form the n texts.
- `cAo`: `A72o` against `A80o`. `cCo`: `C72o` against `P12o`. `cLo`: `L72o` against `P12o`. The three comparisons come from `facts_text.py` [Ref1].
- `c['oldL']` (line 490). `near`: the lowest rate of the pool minus the highest rate of part L, in GB/s. `near_pct`: `near` as a percent of that lowest pool rate. `mid`: the pool median minus the part L median. `mid_pct`: `mid` as a percent of the pool median.
- Present values: 1.24 GB/s (0.3 %) at the nearest ends and 6.27 GB/s (1.3 %) between the medians [Ref4].
- `by['Bo']`, `by['gaps']`, `by['near']`: the oldread range of the pool processes that started after 120-thread work, their gaps in seconds, and the distance of part L below them (line 563).
- `pcv`, `oth`: part C in that view (line 580) and the other-binary rows (line 609).
- Rates print with 2 decimal places (`g`, `sp`). Percent values print with 1 decimal place (`pc`).

Checks and values for the verdict of the new read kernel.
- The build stops unless `newread` holds round 1 and round 2, and all 3 session-1 intervals of each round lie above the 8000 MT/s range of that round.
- `rounds`: per round, the smallest and the largest value of `above`. One value of `above` is the rate of a session-1 interval minus `b80['hi']`. `b80['hi']` is the highest rate of rows A-1 and A-2 in the same round [Ref1].
- `n72r`, `n80r`: n of each round as text. The build stops unless both rounds give the same text.
- `kAw`: the part C group asmread after oldread (`Aao`, line 988) against the pool L-1 to L-4 without the interval that holds the error records.
- The build stops unless three conditions hold. The two ranges do not overlap. The distance `kAw['dist']` is above 0 (the part C group is the higher range). The distance equals the distance to the whole pool (`kAao`, line 1015).
- `allv`: now the range of asmread over the three visits. In line 1045 the name was a list.

segments.heading: Verdict text for the new read kernel
segments.text:
The template of `V['q2_new_read']`, the Q2 verdict for the new read kernel. Lines 1355 to 1357 hold its first statement, on part A (bw_new read, session 1).
- The statement: outside the 8000 MT/s range of the same round in both rounds, with the text `rounds` and n of each round. No percent is given.
- The next sentence is typed in the template: "The pass counts differ, so part A gives no exact size." Lines 762 to 770 print the pass counts in section 4.3.
- No check compares the pass counts of the 7200 MT/s intervals with those of the 8000 MT/s intervals. In facts.json the 6 session-1 intervals of bw_new read have 664 passes each. Of the 12 bw_new read intervals of rows A-1 and A-2, 9 have 600 passes. The other 3 have 603, 663 and 664 passes.

The rest of the template. Its statements, in order:
- Part L (asmread) and the part C group asmread after oldread: the wording of the range test and both ranges.
- The interval with the hardware error records, and the 8000 MT/s range without it.
- Part C, kernel read: the fixed text `NO_READ`.
- F72d12: its asmread range, the words that it lies inside the range of the pool, and its distance above L-1 alone. Control I: its asmread range, and its distances above the pool and above L-1 alone.
- The span of the three visits (`allv`), the six distances of `dist`, and the text `ins` of rule V1 point 3.

The values for the template, in the order of the text. No new rate and no new distance is computed. `nns` and `nn` form the n texts.
- `cLa`: `L72a` against `P12a`. `kAao`: `Aao` against `P12a`. Each gives its wording, both ranges and `dist`.
- `c['hw']['low_a']`: the asmread interval of the pool with the lowest rate. `c['hw']['wo']`: the range of the pool without it (line 916).
- `cFa['a']`, `cIa['a']`: the asmread ranges of F72d12 and of control I.
- `kF1['dist']`, `kI1['dist']`: the distances of these two rows above L-1 alone. `cIa['dist']`: the distance of control I above the pool.
- `allv` and the six values of `dist` from section 4.6.
- Earlier checks stop the build unless the fixed words hold: part L above the pool [Ref1], control I above the pool (line 889), F72d12 and control I above L-1 alone (line 891), F72d12 inside the pool (line 1158), the part C group above the pool (line 1351). More checks: the positions of asmread in the part C group and in rows L-1 to L-4 (line 999), the order of the distances (line 1150), and no change of a wording without the interval with error records (lines 918 and 1351). The count "Two" of the error records is typed in the template. Lines 245, 291 and 298 test the sentence that holds it.
`V['q2']` is the two verdict texts joined with one space. Both texts are written to the sheet as two paragraphs with bold labels.

`V['same_boot']`: the values of section 4.6 as an object for facts.json. It starts with a kernel label, the boot id and the memory speed from `try6`.
- `F72d12`, `part_L`, `control_I`: the lowest and the highest asmread rate of each visit. `pool_8000_L1_to_L4`: the same for `P12a`.
- `spread_GBps`: `spread`, rounded to 3 decimal places. `distance_part_L_to_pool_GBps`: `cLa['dist']`, rounded in the same way.
- `part_L_above_F72d12_GBps`, `part_L_above_pool_8000_GBps`: the three boot distances and the three pool distances of `dist`.
- `F72d12_process_list`: the path and the time of env.txt, the launch time, the load at launch, and the entries of the process list.
- `build_facts.py` rounds every decimal number of `V` to 3 places when it writes facts.json [Ref3].

`V['pool_8000_by_start_state']`: the view by start state of section 4.2 as an object for facts.json. No new value is computed.
- `below_load_1`, `after_120_thread_work`: the two groups of the pool L-1 to L-4. Each holds its processes, the lowest and the highest oldread and asmread rate, and the numbers of intervals and processes. These two numbers come from the oldread list.
- `part_L_oldread_below_second_group_GBps`, `part_L_asmread_above_second_group_GBps`: `by['near']` and `by['asm_near']`.
- `part_C`: the start state, the loads, the oldread range and the counts of all part C intervals. Then the oldread range and the interval count of the cfwd intervals at position 0. Each of the two ranges has its distance below the second group.
- The two `overlaps_...` flags are the constant `True`. The checks in lines 577 and 606 stop the build before this point when an overlap is missing.

- `other_binary_after_120_thread_work`: the 8000 MT/s processes of bwx11 and of runner bwx that started after a 120-thread process. Each entry holds processes or rows, gaps or loads, the oldread range at position 0 and the counts.
- The flag `part_C_oldread_overlaps` is the constant `True`. The check in line 606 stops the build before this point when the overlap is missing.
- `part_L_below_every_oldread_interval_8000_12_modules`: the highest oldread rate of part L, and the lowest oldread rate of all 8000 MT/s records with 12 modules. It also holds the row and the process of that lowest record, and the number of such intervals (lines 604 to 611).

`V['part_A_thread_rates']`: one entry per cell `t` of `c['thr']` from section 4.3 (line 869). Both values are in GB/s.
- `t['est']`: 120 x (the lowest `per_thread_avg_GBps` of the session-1 intervals minus the highest `per_thread_avg_GBps` of rows A-1 and A-2 in the same round). It is an estimate (est.) of the nearest-end distance. It is rounded to 1 decimal place.
- `t['agg']`: the smallest value of `above` of the cell (line 830). That is the lowest session-1 rate above the 8000 MT/s range of the round, minus the highest rate of that range, by the column `aggregate_GBps`. It is rounded to 2 decimal places.

segments.heading: Section 5: record-only table of part A
segments.text:
Writes the heading and two notes.
- The interval length in the first note comes from `secs` over all part A records of the rerun (0.5 s in the present sheet [Ref4]).
- For a part A record the field `min_ms` is the constant 500 (in ms) that `build_facts.py` sets. It is not read from the csv file. An integrity check of `build_facts.py` tests that the part A script ra.sh starts the binary with the options `--reps 3 --min-ms 500` [Ref3].
- The notes say that no statement is made from these rows. They also say that the copy kernels count read plus written bytes. This file does not compute that count. `build_facts.py` stops unless the header line that the binary prints for each copy and asmcopy process of part A and of rows A-1 to A-3 holds the words `copy counts read+write bytes` [Ref3].

One table row per kernel (write, copy, asmwrite, asmcopy) and binary (bw_old, bw_new). Four data columns: row A-1, and sessions 1, 2 and 3 of part A of the rerun.
- `sel` takes every record of that binary and kernel in the row or session. Both rounds go into one cell.
- A cell prints n, then the lowest, the median and the highest `GBps`, with 2 decimal places.
- In facts.json every cell has n = 6: 3 intervals of each of the 2 rounds.

segments.heading: Section 6: established, not established, hypotheses
segments.text: Writes the heading. `nck` is the number of integrity checks in `D['checks']`. The build stops unless every check has a true `ok` field.

Counts in how many load-only cells of part A round 2 lies above round 1.
- A cell is one session (1, 2 or 3) and one of bw_new read, bw_old asmread and bw_new asmread. That gives 9 cells.
- `a1_`: the records of the cell in round 1. `a2_`: the records in round 2. In facts.json each list is one process with 3 intervals.
- `r2` increases by 1 when the lowest rate of round 2 is above the highest rate of round 1. Then the two ranges do not overlap.
- In the present sheet `r2` is 8 of 9 cells [Ref4].

`est` is the list of the established points. Items 1 to 4:
- Item 1: the boot id, MemTotal and the time of the 12-module reading, from `try6`. Its words "in every state line" are typed in the template. The integrity checks `boot` and `memtotal` of `build_facts.py` compare the boot id and MemTotal of every state line with try6.txt [Ref3]. Item 2: the number of checks.
- Item 3: Q1 in fixed words. `facts_text.py` checks it before it calls `section4`: the build stops there unless every pair has a drop above 0 % [Ref1].
- Item 4: the size of the Q1 drop. A drop is (1 - rate of the load-only kernel / rate of oldread) x 100. Both intervals come from the same process and round [Ref1].
- `pcr` prints the lowest and the highest drop of a list, with 1 decimal place. When both round to the same text, it prints one value. `c['dl']`, `c['di']` and `c['df']` hold the asmread drops of part L, of control I and of F72d12. `CG[...][1]` holds the drops of one part C group.
- Present values: 29.2 % to 30.5 % in part L, and 35.4 % in F72d12 [Ref4].

Items 5 and 6, the Q2 results.
- Item 5, old read kernel: prints `c['oldL']['near']` and `c['oldL']['mid']`. These are the distances of part L below the pool L-1 to L-4, at the nearest ends and between the medians.
- Item 5 also prints the number of pool processes that started after 120-thread work, and `pcv['near']`, the distance of part C below them.
- Item 6, load-only loop: fixed words with the label `ADDED`. No value is inserted.
- Checks stop the build unless the data show what the two items state. Item 5: checks in `facts_text.py` (the overlaps, and part L below the pool) [Ref1], and lines 577 and 606 (part C). Item 6: line 748 (part A), one check in `facts_text.py` (part L) [Ref1], line 889 (control I) and line 1351 (part C).

- Item 7: the asmread ranges of F72d12 and of part L, with their launch times.
- Item 8: `r2` and `cells` from line 1462.
- Item 9: the mesh result of section 4.7, with the three interval counts of `c['mesh']`.
- Item 9 says in fixed words which mesh sums are higher, which are lower and which ranges overlap. The checks in lines 1253, 1256, 1259 and 1275 test these words.

Items 10 and 11 have fixed words. The loop writes the items as a numbered list, 1 to 11.
- Item 10: line 219 stops the build unless the F72d12 process lies between two readings of the same boot id.
- Item 11: the two counts of 2 records are typed in the template. Lines 245 and 291 to 302 test them and the two intervals. Lines 918 and 1351 test that no wording changes without the first interval.

segments.heading: Section 6: list of what is not established
segments.text: `hwx` is the result of the comparison of intervals with hardware error records (line 372). `sgn` prints a difference in GB/s with 2 decimal places and its sign. A value that rounds to zero prints as `0.00`.

`notest` is the list of the points that are not established. Items 1 to 4:
- Item 1: the text `ins` of line 1195.
- Item 2: fixed words on the three visits.
- Item 3: the oldread ranges of part L and of control I. Then the oldread ranges and n of the two start-state groups of the pool (`by['Bo']`, `by['Io']`). The check in line 557 tests the words "gave higher oldread values".
- Item 4: `NO_READ`, and the run that would resolve it.

Items 5 to 10. Each names one thing that is not known. Items 5 to 9 have fixed words. Item 10 inserts one value: `c['fw']['readable']`, the number of readable values in the saved list of firmware settings [Ref1].

Item 11, the comparison of intervals with hardware error records. `diff` is the rate of such an interval minus the rate of the same kernel at the same position in the other round of the same process.
- `hwx['n']`: the number of intervals to which records can be assigned. `hwx['low']`: those with `diff` below -1.0 GB/s (`hwx['lim']` is 1.0 GB/s). `hwx['rest']`: the others. Line 359 stops the build unless every `diff` of `rest` is below 1.0 GB/s as an absolute value.
- The text prints the `low` differences as positive numbers, smallest first. Then it prints the lowest and the highest `diff` of `rest` with their signs.
- `hwx['cmax']`: the position without records where the two rounds differ most. Its `diff` prints as an absolute value.
- Present values: 8 intervals. 3 of them are 1.96, 3.69 and 10.07 GB/s lower. Without records the rounds differ by up to 6.24 GB/s [Ref4].

`V['insufficient_data']` is set to `notest`. Until this line the list held only the entry that line 1199 appended. The text `ins` stays in the list as item 1. The loop writes the items as a numbered list.

segments.heading: Section 6: hypotheses H1 to H5
segments.text:
Data for hypothesis H1 from two 8000 MT/s rows.
- `r0`: the asmread records of the processes p1 and p2 of row R0 (bwx11). The selection has no position condition. For row R0, `build_facts.py` keeps only oldread at position 0 and asmread at position 1 as records [Ref3]. The csv files of p1 and p2 also hold asmread at position 10. These intervals are not used.
- `l2`: the asmread intervals at position 1 of the processes p1nop and p2add of row L-2. `l2load`: their loads at launch.
- The build stops unless every asmread rate of p2add is below every asmread rate of p1nop.
- It also stops unless p2add was launched at a load above 1 and p1nop at a load below 1.

`hyp` is the list of the five hypotheses. These lines are the template of H1 (start state). It names what fits, what does not fit, and the measurement that would confirm or reject the hypothesis. Lines 1581 to 1589 give the values for its placeholders.
- Checks test the words of this text that compare rates: lines 557 and 558 (the two start-state groups of the pool), line 1563 (row L-2) and line 1609 (part A).
- oldread of part L below control I: two checks of `facts_text.py` together show it. Part L lies below the pool L-1 to L-4, and control I lies inside the range of that pool [Ref1].
- No check tests the words "below p1" for row R0. In facts.json the asmread rates of p2 (296.02 and 296.22 GB/s) are below the rates of p1 (302.59 and 303.16 GB/s).

The values of H1, in the order of the text. The ranges of part L, of control I, of row R0 and of part A are formed here with `rng`. `sp` prints a range as the lowest to the highest `GBps`.
- Part L: the gap of T72L1 after part A, and the asmread range. Control I: the asmread range.
- `r2`, `cells`: the count of line 1462.
- Row R0: the load at launch and the asmread range of p2 and of p1.
- The two start-state groups of the pool (`by`): process counts, gaps, names, loads, asmread ranges and n. Then row L-2: the loads and the single asmread rates of p2add and of p1nop.
- oldread: the ranges of the same two groups, of part L and of control I.
- Part A: the bw_new read range of the round-1 process of sessions 1, 2 and 3 (`N['pa'][0]`, `[2]`, `[4]`), and the gap of T72A2 after 120-thread work. The text applies this one gap to sessions 2 and 3. These lines do not read the gap of T72A3. In facts.json that gap is also 5 s.

H2 (time since boot). No rate is used.
- The two time values are a launch time minus the time of the first Linux kernel log line of the boot, printed by `dur`. One is for F72d12. The other is for the first process of the rerun (`T72A1`).
- The limit sentence prints the first entry of the F72d12 process list again.
- The words "gave the lowest values" are typed in the template. The check in line 1048 tests them for asmread against part L and control I.

H3 and H5 have fixed words.
- H4 inserts the pass count `64 * 6 + 56 * 5` = 664 passes. That is 6 passes on each of the 64 threads of mesh 0 plus 5 passes on each of the 56 threads of mesh 1.
- The text says that this split is not proven. The reason it gives: threads120.csv has no row per thread.

Two checks for sentences of the hypotheses. The build stops unless both hold.
- H4: at least one bw_new read record of part A of the rerun has 664 in its field `passes`. In facts.json 16 of the 18 such records have 664 passes.
- H1: the entries 0, 2 and 4 of `N['pa']` belong to sessions 1, 2 and 3, and entry 0 is round 1. The lowest bw_new read rate of entry 0 must be above the highest rate of entries 2 and 4.
`V['hypotheses']` is set to `hyp`. Each hypothesis is written as one bullet. The function `section4` ends here, and the file ends too. The function returns nothing.
